sources.citation: ISO 639-3 Registration Authority. 2012. Change Request Number 2012-034: [nrr] Norra > Nora, Living (Myanmar) > Extinct (Northeast India); adopted 2013-01-23. SIL International, 5 pp.
sources.note: Nothing on stress or phonology; an administrative form. Rationale (p.2): Norra is 'usually spelled Nora and is an extinct Tai-Kadai language of northeast India'; Bradley (p.c. 2012): 'Norra is an old alternative name for a Tai group of NE India whose language is also known as Khamyang'; Shafer's Bibliography of Sino-Tibetan p.142 calls Norra a variety of Khamti Shan. Sources named: Somsonge Burusphat (ed.) 1998 Introduction to Tai-Kadai People; Diller 1992; Grierson 1903 LSI.

Nothing on stress. Justification note: entry retired; the original listing (Nora, Byabe, Kizolo) derives from Voegelin & Voegelin 1965 and these are dialects of Nung; Sun & Liu 2009 report Nung in China and Nung across the border in Myanmar are mutually intelligible. Zero descriptive references.
